app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

Hypothesis: frontend-proxy's Envoy route/upstream config is misconfigured so that an upstream cluster resolves or routes back to the proxy (or uses the wrong host/header), producing repeated proxy -> frontend -> proxy hops and inflated latency. Confirm proxy-side routing, active clusters, and any route-to-host mappings or errors in the proxy logs.

Hypothesis: frontend-proxy is configured to forward to a backend hostname/port that does not match the frontend Service/Pods (wrong service name/port or host header), causing requests to be redirected back to the proxy. Verify proxy route/cluster entries and the frontend Service spec/endpoints/port to ensure exact host:port/name match.

Classification: dependency/config (application-level outbound config). Hypothesis: frontend application is configured to call an upstream using a URL/hostname that resolves to the proxy (or the proxy's service name) instead of the intended backend, causing frontend to send requests back through frontend-proxy and creating a loop. Inspect frontend pod environment, startup logs and outgoing call logs to capture the target hostnames/URLs.

1) get_pods_from_service(frontend-proxy) showed a single healthy pod: frontend-proxy-7f7946c995-sxs4s (Running). This confirms logs from the single active proxy instance were examined.

Therefore the hypothesis that the frontend-proxy config is misrouting requests back to the proxy is not supported by the proxy-side logs. Further troubleshooting should examine client-side routing, service discovery entries, or upstream service configurations (e.g., cluster definitions in the control plane) since the proxy itself shows normal initialization and no routing-loop errors.
